title: Headless child inherits parent CLAUDE_* session env (strip is a blocklist, not an allowlist)
description: Observed in the CAM-516 real-binary ceremony (2026-08-09, claude 2.1.226, unsandboxed): buildHeadlessChildEnv removes CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, TMUX and TMUX_PANE, but the child was still born with CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT and AI_AGENT inherited from the parent process. CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION point at the PARENT session. The ceremony ran in the worst case (launched from inside a live claude session) and still closed exit 0, so this is not fatal, but the project has already been bitten by nested-environment poisoning (CAM-43), where inherited session variables killed the worker. Round 4 of the CAM-516 review adjudicated this FILAR SEPARADO, not a ship blocker. The design question to settle: the strip should probably be an allowlist (pass through only what the child needs) rather than a blocklist that has to enumerate every upstream variable Anthropic may add. Entry point: src/supervisor/headless-argv.ts around the child env builder.
